hypotheses: Belinostat is a hydroxamic acid HDAC inhibitor; its A375 anchor profile is dominated by increased H3K18ac1K23ac1 and H3K9ac1K14ac1 with decreased H3K9me2K14ac0, H3K9me1K14ac0, H3K9me3K14ac0, and H3K27me0K36me2, consistent with a histone acetylation/repressive-methylation perturbation.

RGFP966 (HDAC3-selective inhibitor) has the highest anchor similarity (0.5657) and structure similarity (0.3) among candidates, so its donor response may best reproduce the belinostat acetylation signature.

Decitabine (DNMT inhibitor) and tacrolimus (calcineurin inhibitor) have moderate anchor similarity but non-HDAC mechanisms; they are lower-priority donors for a reproducible histone acetylation perturbation.
Geldanamycin (HSP90 inhibitor) and bortezomib (proteasome inhibitor) have moderate anchor similarity but are unlikely to directly produce the same HDAC-inhibitor-like histone mark pattern.

The fixed decoder selects a target cell/feature/sign; the ridge diagnostic (PC3, BI10036, H3K27me1K36me1, sign -1) and phenotype/chemical diagnostics (MCF7, BI10031, H3K18ac1K23ac1, sign +1) suggest the transfer may be driven by H3K18ac1K23ac1 gain and H3K27me1K36me1 loss.
object.evidence_gap: No query_sources are provided, so the belinostat anchor profile is not linked to measured donor responses; donor pharmacology descriptions and measured target-minus-A375 responses are needed to verify whether any candidate donor produces a >0.5 log2 histone perturbation versus vehicle.
